concerns.concern: A higher effective conductivity does not by itself show a performance advantage, because output scales with σ^eff·S². The transverse SSE coefficient here (~10–17 nV/K) is about an order of magnitude below typical YIG/Pt values, and no power-factor comparison with conventional devices is given. The claim that this demonstrates a trans-scale SSE is therefore not established.
concerns.quote: High σ^eff alone does not demonstrate a performance advantage; no power-factor comparison with conventional devices

concerns.concern: The magnetization argument cannot exclude ferromagnetic impurities. Dilution by the sputtered Pt would mask a few wt% of Fe-based phases, the XRD detection limit is not stated, and the noisy Hall data could hide a small anomalous component. The sign of the signal relative to the known YIG/Pt LSSE sign is also not reported.
concerns.quote: A few wt% of Fe₃O₄ or FePt would raise M_s by only a few percent and would be completely masked by that dilution.

concerns.concern: S_SSE barely changes (~15–20%) when the Pt thickness doubles and σ^eff rises 4–6×. The bilayer shunting picture predicts roughly halving, so the claimed consistency with conventional thickness dependence, used to support the SSE assignment, does not hold.
concerns.quote: The direction matches, but the magnitude is far from the conventional expectation.

concerns.concern: The isotropy claim rests on a single sample measured in two configurations with different thermal contacts. The orientation of the pressing axis relative to the measurement axes is not stated, so the 3% agreement may be partly coincidental.
concerns.quote: Isotropy claim rests on one sample, two different thermal setups, and an unspecified pressing axis

concerns.concern: The '2–3 orders of magnitude' higher conductivity claim exceeds what Table S1 supports. The weakest composite is only ~10× above the best conventional device, and conventional σ^eff depends on an arbitrary substrate thickness.
concerns.quote: The weakest composite (15-RT, 562 S/m) versus the best conventional device (53 S/m) is only ~10×, i.e. one order of magnitude.

concerns.concern: The magnetization values plotted in Fig. 3f and Fig. S6 are about three orders of magnitude smaller than the quoted 37.9 emu/g. That quoted value matches low-temperature rather than 300 K YIG magnetization.
concerns.quote: That is about three orders of magnitude smaller.

concerns.concern: The 15-nm and 30-nm samples show similar magnetization reductions, even though doubling the Pt thickness should roughly double the dilution. This needs explanation.
concerns.quote: the 15-nm and 30-nm samples show similar M_s reductions. Doubling the Pt thickness should roughly double the dilution

concerns.concern: Key fabrication and geometry details are missing: powder size distribution, loaded mass, deposition times, verification of the 15/30-nm Pt thickness, pressing hold time and direction, and sample/electrode dimensions. Particle size is central to the trans-scale concept and to the Pt volume fraction.
concerns.quote: Key fabrication and geometry parameters are unspecified

concerns.concern: Saying the signal originates 'purely' from YIG's SSE is overstated. The authors concede that α-Fe₂O₃ and YFeO₃ could not be distinguished by XRD, and the impurity-exclusion arguments have limited sensitivity.
concerns.quote: the observed signals originate purely from the SSE of YIG

concerns.concern: Trends across processing conditions, such as RT versus 300 °C pressing, are drawn from single samples of a single batch. The S_SSE values in the text and Fig. S5 carry no uncertainties, so the ~2× difference cannot be distinguished from variability, and it is not explained mechanistically.
concerns.quote: All properties reported in this study were measured from samples prepared in a single batch.

concerns.concern: Relative density is computed against pure YIG and ignores the much denser Pt, so the true relative density is lower (~64%). The paper also treats porosity effects on κ as proportional to density, which undermines the argument that low κ cannot be explained by density alone.
concerns.quote: Pt (21.45 g/cm³) raises the theoretical density of the composite.

concerns.concern: Low thermal conductivity is attributed to interfacial phonon scattering without considering inter-particle contact resistance in the cold-pressed samples. The laser-flash measurement direction relative to the pressing axis and the SSE gradient is also not stated, so κ may be anisotropic.
concerns.quote: Constriction and contact resistance between particles is the more obvious explanation for κ well below porosity-corrected values.

concerns.concern: The measured specific heat of the Pt-containing composites exceeds that of pure YIG, though Pt should lower it. This implies a ~10% DSC uncertainty that propagates into κ but is not reported.
concerns.quote: This indicates a DSC uncertainty of order ±10%.

concerns.concern: Being thicker than the spin diffusion length is conflated with Pt continuity. Continuity is set by the island-to-film transition, and exceeding λ_s actually reduces the ISHE voltage through shunting.
concerns.quote: Being above λ_s actually reduces the ISHE voltage through shunting rather than 'ensuring clear observation'.

concerns.concern: XRD references are inconsistent. One PDF card number is assigned to both Y₂O₃ and FePt, though the FePt lines are used to exclude an impurity. The Cu-Kα wavelength differs between Methods and Note S2, and Note S2 cites the wrong figure for the XRD data.
concerns.quote: PDF#43-0661 is assigned to both Y₂O₃ and FePt (Note S2 and the Fig. S3 legend), so one card number is wrong.

concerns.concern: The isotropy sentence compares the Hx-∇zT result with itself due to a configuration label error. It should refer to the Hz-∇xT configuration.
concerns.quote: As written, the comparison underpinning the isotropy claim is self-referential.
